content: Nin Jiom Pei Pa Koa, also known as King-to Nin Jiom Pei Pa Koa (京 都 念 慈 菴 川 貝 枇 杷 膏), or simply Pei Pa Koa, is a traditional Chinese herbal remedy. It is specifically formulated to alleviate symptoms such as sore throat, coughing, hoarseness, and loss of voice. This preparation functions as both a throat demulcent and an expectorant. Currently, it is manufactured and distributed globally by Nin Jiom Medicine Manufactory Limited, a company based in Hong Kong. The name King-to refers to capital, symbolizing Beijing, while Nin Jiom translates to in memory of my mother. The term Pei Pa Koa means loquat syrup. History The original formula for Pei Pa Koa was developed by Dr. Ip Tin-See, a physician during the Qing Dynasty. He created the remedy at the request of Yang Xiao-Lian, a provincial commander, to treat his mother’s persistent cough. The effectiveness of the formula impressed the Yang family so much that they established a factory to mass-produce it. Eventually, the Yang family sold the business to Tse Sui-Bong, a practitioner of medicine. In 1962, Nin Jiom Medicine Manufacturing was officially incorporated to expand the business. Today, Pei Pa Koa generates annual sales of approximately 45 million USD. Effectiveness A study conducted by the China Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine, published in a 1994 article titled Pharmacological studies of Nin Jiom Pei Pa Koa, demonstrated that Pei Pa Koa has significant therapeutic effects. It was shown to effectively relieve coughing, facilitate the removal of sputum, and alleviate asthma symptoms in both in vivo and in vitro settings. Composition Pei Pa Koa is composed of a blend of herbal ingredients, each selected for its specific medicinal properties. These include: Fritillaria bulb (Chuan Bei Mu): Known for its ability to clear heat and resolve phlegm. Loquat leaf (Pi Pa Ye): Traditionally used to soothe the throat and reduce coughing. Ladybell root (Nan Sha Shen): Helps to nourish the lungs and alleviate dryness. Poria cocos (Fu Ling): Aids in promoting fluid metabolism and calming the mind. Pomelo peel (Mao Ju Hong): Used to regulate qi and improve digestion. Chinese bellflower root (Jie Geng): Facilitates the expulsion of phlegm and supports respiratory health. Pinellia rhizome (Ban Xia): Known for its ability to dry dampness and resolve phlegm. Schisandra chinensis seed (Wu Wei Zi): Helps to astringe the lungs and reduce coughing. Trichosanthes seed (Gua Lou Zi): Used to clear heat and moisten the lungs. Coltsfoot flower (Guan Dong Hua): Soothes the throat and relieves coughing. Thinleaf milkwort root (Yuan Zhi): Supports respiratory function and calms the mind. Bitter apricot kernel (Ku Xing Ren): Known for its antitussive and expectorant properties. Fresh ginger (Shen Jiang): Warms the lungs and alleviates nausea. Licorice root (Gan Cao): Harmonizes the formula and provides soothing effects. These herbal components are combined in a syrup and honey base, which enhances the palatability and therapeutic efficacy of the preparation.
